nodes.statement_short: Split on whether $s_0\in T_{[a,t_0)}$.

nodes.name: Case $s_0\in T_{[a,t_0)}$
nodes.statement: Suppose $s_0\in T_{[a,t_0)}$. Hence $s_0=\max T_{[a,t_0)}<t_0$, and so, $T_{[a,t_0)}=T_{[a,s_0]}$ and $T_{[s_0,t_0]}=\{s_0,t_0\}$ (two-point set). By the additivity of~$\mbox{\rm V}$, \begin{align*} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,s_0]})+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[s_0,t_0]}) \\[2pt] &=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})+d_H(\Gamma_1(s_0),\Gamma_2(t_0)), \end{align*} which implies \begin{align*} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\\[2pt] &=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})+d_H(\Gamma_1(s_0),\Gamma_2(t_0)) +\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_2,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\\[2pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})+d_H(\Gamma(s_0),\Gamma(t_0))+{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[t_0,+\infty)}). \end{align*} This proves inequality \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:s1t0})} with $J_a(\Gamma,t_0)=d_H(\Gamma(s_0),\Gamma(t_0))$ from \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:J})}.
nodes.statement_short: Two-point additivity gives the bound with $J_a=d_H(\Gamma(s_0),\Gamma(t_0))$.

nodes.name: Case $s_0\notin T_{[a,t_0)}$
nodes.statement:
Now, suppose $s_0
otin T_{[a,t_0)}$. Note that $s_0$ is a left limit point of $T_{[a,s_0)}$ (and so, of $T_{[a,t_0)}$ and $T$ as well). In fact, by the definition of $s_0$, $t<s_0$ for all $t\in T_{[a,s_0)}$, and, given $\varepsilon>0$, there is $t_\varepsilon\in T_{[a,s_0)}$ such that $s_0-\varepsilon<t_\varepsilon$. Hence $s_0-\varepsilon<t_\varepsilon<s_0$, i.e., $T_{[a,s_0)}\cap(s_0-\varepsilon,s_0)
e\varnothing$ (and a fortiori $T\cap(s_0-\varepsilon,s_0)
e\varnothing$). Let us show that the limit in the right-hand side of \mbox{m(ef{e:J})} exists in $[0,+\infty)$. Since $\Gamma=\Gamma_1$ on $T_{[a,t_0)}$ and $\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})$, given $t,t'\in T_{[a,s_0)}$ with $t\le t'$, the additivity of $\mbox{m V}$ implies (note again that $a=\min T$)  egin{align*} 0&\le\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})-\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t',t_0]})=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t']}) \[2pt] &=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t']})-\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t]}). \end{align*} By \mbox{m(ef{e:ttos})}, the right-hand side here tends to $\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})-\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})=0$ as $T
i t,t'	o s_0-0$, and so, Cauchy's criterion yields the existence of the~limit. Applying the additivity of $\mbox{m V}$ once again, we get  egin{equation} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]}) \quad\mbox{for all \,$t\in T_{[a,s_0)}$.} \end{equation} Noting that $s_0
otin T_{[a,t_0)}$ implies $T_{[a,s_0)}=T_{[a,t_0)}$, by virtue of \mbox{m(ef{e:ttos})}, the limit of the first term in \mbox{m(ef{e:star})} as $T
i t	o s_0-0$ is equal to  egin{align*} \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})&= \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t]})= \mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})\[2pt] &=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)}). \end{align*} Taking into account \mbox{m(ef{e:J})}, it follows from \mbox{m(ef{e:star})} that  egin{align*} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\[2pt] &=\lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\!\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})+ \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\!\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})+ \mbox{m V}(\Gamma_2,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\ &=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})+J_a(\Gamma,t_0)+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_2,T_{[t_0,+\infty)}) \[2pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})+J_a(\Gamma,t_0)+{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[t_0,+\infty)}). \end{align*} This proves the first inequality in \mbox{m(ef{e:s1t0})}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $J_a$ exists as a limit and bound $V(\Gamma,T)$ via (e:star).

nodes.name: $s_0$ is a left limit point
nodes.statement: Note that $s_0$ is a left limit point of $T_{[a,s_0)}$ (and so, of $T_{[a,t_0)}$ and $T$ as well). In fact, by the definition of $s_0$, $t<s_0$ for all $t\in T_{[a,s_0)}$, and, given $\varepsilon>0$, there is $t_\varepsilon\in T_{[a,s_0)}$ such that $s_0-\varepsilon<t_\varepsilon$. Hence $s_0-\varepsilon<t_\varepsilon<s_0$, i.e., $T_{[a,s_0)}\cap(s_0-\varepsilon,s_0)\ne\varnothing$ (and a fortiori $T\cap(s_0-\varepsilon,s_0)\ne\varnothing$).
nodes.statement_short: By definition of $s_0$ as a supremum.

nodes.name: Existence of the limit in (e:J)
nodes.statement: Let us show that the limit in the right-hand side of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:J})} exists in $[0,+\infty)$. Since $\Gamma=\Gamma_1$ on $T_{[a,t_0)}$ and $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})$, given $t,t'\in T_{[a,s_0)}$ with $t\le t'$, the additivity of $\mbox{\rm V}$ implies (note again that $a=\min T$) \begin{align*} 0&\le\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t',t_0]})=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t']}) \\[2pt] &=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t']})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t]}). \end{align*} By \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:ttos})}, the right-hand side here tends to $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})=0$ as $T\ni t,t'\to s_0-0$, and so, Cauchy's criterion yields the existence of the~limit.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy criterion via additivity and (e:ttos).

nodes.name: Cauchy differences
nodes.statement: Since $\Gamma=\Gamma_1$ on $T_{[a,t_0)}$ and $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})$, given $t,t'\in T_{[a,s_0)}$ with $t\le t'$, the additivity of $\mbox{\rm V}$ implies (note again that $a=\min T$) \begin{align*} 0&\le\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t',t_0]})=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t']}) \\[2pt] &=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t']})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t]}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differences of tail variations are variations of $\Gamma_1$ on middle segments.

nodes.name: Cauchy criterion
nodes.statement: By \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:ttos})}, the right-hand side here tends to $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})-\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})=0$ as $T\ni t,t'\to s_0-0$, and so, Cauchy's criterion yields the existence of the~limit.
nodes.statement_short: Differences tend to 0, so the limit exists.

nodes.name: Bound via (e:star)
nodes.statement:
Applying the additivity of $\mbox{m V}$ once again, we get  egin{equation} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]}) \quad\mbox{for all \,$t\in T_{[a,s_0)}$.} \end{equation} Noting that $s_0
otin T_{[a,t_0)}$ implies $T_{[a,s_0)}=T_{[a,t_0)}$, by virtue of \mbox{m(ef{e:ttos})}, the limit of the first term in \mbox{m(ef{e:star})} as $T
i t	o s_0-0$ is equal to  egin{align*} \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})&= \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{(-\infty,t]})= \mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,s_0)})\[2pt] &=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)}). \end{align*} Taking into account \mbox{m(ef{e:J})}, it follows from \mbox{m(ef{e:star})} that  egin{align*} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\[2pt] &=\lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\!\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t]})+ \lim_{T
i t	o s_0-0}\!\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})+ \mbox{m V}(\Gamma_2,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\ &=\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_1,T_{[a,t_0)})+J_a(\Gamma,t_0)+\mbox{m V}(\Gamma_2,T_{[t_0,+\infty)}) \[2pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})+J_a(\Gamma,t_0)+{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T_{[t_0,+\infty)}). \end{align*} This proves the first inequality in \mbox{m(ef{e:s1t0})}.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit in (e:star) to obtain the first inequality.

nodes.name: Remaining: jump interpretation
nodes.statement: It remains to show that if $s_0=t_0$, then $J_a(\Gamma,t_0)$ is the left jump of $\Gamma$ at~$t_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing $J_a$ is the left jump when $s_0=t_0$.

nodes.name: $J_a$ equals the left jump
nodes.statement:
Noting that, by the additivity of $\mbox{m V}$,  egin{equation*} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]})=\ori{v}(t_0)-\ori{v}(t)\quad\mbox{for all \,$t\in T_{[a,t_0)}$,} \end{equation*} and, by \mbox{m(ef{e:VFtm})},  egin{equation*} \ori{v}(t_0)=\ori{v}(t_0-0)+\lim_{T
i t	o t_0-0}d_H(\Gamma(t),\Gamma(t_0)), \end{equation*} and passing to the limit as $T
i t	o t_0-0$, we get  egin{align*} J_a(\Gamma,t_0)&=\lim_{T
i t	o t_0-0}\mbox{m V}(\Gamma,T_{[t,t_0]}) =\ori{v}(t_0)-\lim_{T
i t	o t_0-0}\ori{v}(t)\ &=\ori{v}(t_0-0)+\lim_{T
i t	o t_0-0}d_H(\Gamma(t),\Gamma(t_0))-\ori{v}(t_0-0)\ &=\lim_{T
i t	o t_0-0}d_H(\Gamma(t),\Gamma(t_0)). \end{align*} This completes the proof of Theorem~ef{t:BV}. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Additivity and the jump formula (e:VFtm) give $J_a$ as the left jump.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem A from Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Setting $T_+=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}$ and $T_-=T_{(-\infty,t_0]}$, we have \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_+)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T)\quad\mbox{and}\quad {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_-)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T). \end{equation*} Noting that $t_0\in T_+\cap T_-$ and applying Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a) to $F$ on $T_+$ and Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(b) to $F$ on $T_-$, we obtain a set-valued selector $\Gamma_+:T_+\to\mbox{c}(M)$ of $F$ on $T_+$ and a set-valued selector $\Gamma_-:T_-\to\mbox{c}(M)$ of $F$ on $T_-$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} &d_H(X_0,\Gamma_+(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F(t_0))\quad\!\mbox{and}\quad\! \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_+,T_+)\!\le\!{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+),&\\[2pt] &d_H(\Gamma_+(t_0),\Gamma_-(t_0))\!\le\! e(\Gamma_+(t_0),F(t_0))\!=\!0\quad\! \mbox{and}\!\quad\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_-,T_-)\!\le\!{\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-).& \end{eqnarray*} Noting that $\Gamma_-(t_0)=\Gamma_+(t_0)$, we set $\Gamma(t):=\Gamma_+(t)$ if $t\in T_+$, and $\Gamma(t):=\Gamma_-(t)$ if $t\in T_-\setminus\{t_0\}$. Clearly, $\Gamma:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ is a set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$, $d_H(X_0,\Gamma(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0))$ and, by the additivity of~$\mbox{\rm V}$, \begin{align} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_-)= \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_+,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_-,T_-)\nonumber\\[1pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)+{\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-) \\[2pt] &\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_-)=\mbox{\rm V}(F,T). \nonumber \end{align} This finishes the proof of Theorem~\ref{t:A}. Note that we have shown a little bit more: inequality \mbox{\rm(\ref{RR})} holds provided ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)$ and ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-)$ are finite. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1(a) on $T\cap[t_0,\infty)$ and Theorem 1(b) on $T\cap(-\infty,t_0]$ and glue at $t_0$; additivity of $V$ bounds the variation.

nodes.name: Variation bound (RR)
nodes.statement: \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_-)= \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_+,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_-,T_-)\nonumber\\[1pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)+{\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-) \\[2pt] &\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_-)=\mbox{\rm V}(F,T). \nonumber
nodes.label: RR

nodes.name: Directional variations bounded by $V$
nodes.statement: Setting $T_+=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}$ and $T_-=T_{(-\infty,t_0]}$, we have \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_+)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T)\quad\mbox{and}\quad {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_-)\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Directional variations on both halves are bounded by $V(F,T)$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1 on both halves
nodes.statement: Noting that $t_0\in T_+\cap T_-$ and applying Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a) to $F$ on $T_+$ and Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(b) to $F$ on $T_-$, we obtain a set-valued selector $\Gamma_+:T_+\to\mbox{c}(M)$ of $F$ on $T_+$ and a set-valued selector $\Gamma_-:T_-\to\mbox{c}(M)$ of $F$ on $T_-$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} &d_H(X_0,\Gamma_+(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F(t_0))\quad\!\mbox{and}\quad\! \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_+,T_+)\!\le\!{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+),&\\[2pt] &d_H(\Gamma_+(t_0),\Gamma_-(t_0))\!\le\! e(\Gamma_+(t_0),F(t_0))\!=\!0\quad\! \mbox{and}\!\quad\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_-,T_-)\!\le\!{\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-).& \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1(a) on $T_+$ and 1(b) on $T_-$ with matching value at $t_0$.

nodes.name: Glue the selectors
nodes.statement: Noting that $\Gamma_-(t_0)=\Gamma_+(t_0)$, we set $\Gamma(t):=\Gamma_+(t)$ if $t\in T_+$, and $\Gamma(t):=\Gamma_-(t)$ if $t\in T_-\setminus\{t_0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\Gamma$ piecewise.

nodes.name: Variation bound and conclusion
nodes.statement: Clearly, $\Gamma:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ is a set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$, $d_H(X_0,\Gamma(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0))$ and, by the additivity of~$\mbox{\rm V}$, \begin{align} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_-)= \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_+,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_-,T_-)\nonumber\\[1pt] &\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)+{\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-) \\[2pt] &\le\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_+)+\mbox{\rm V}(F,T_-)=\mbox{\rm V}(F,T). \nonumber \end{align} This finishes the proof of Theorem~\ref{t:A}.
nodes.statement_short: Additivity of $V$ gives $V(\Gamma,T)\le V(F,T)$.

nodes.name: Stronger inequality (RR)
nodes.statement: Note that we have shown a little bit more: inequality \mbox{\rm(\ref{RR})} holds provided ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_+)$ and ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_-)$ are finite. \qed
nodes.statement_short: (RR) holds whenever the two directional variations are finite.

nodes.name: Single-valued selectors of bounded variation
nodes.statement: If $X_0=\{x_0\}\subset M$, a (single-valued) selector of bounded var\-i\-a\-tion $\Gamma:T\!\to\! M$ of $F$ on $T$ may be chosen such that \mbox{$d(x_0,\Gamma(t_0))\!\le\! d(x_0,F(t_0))$} and satisfying the rest of assertions in (a) and (b) of Theorem~\ref{t:BV} (if we replace $d_H$ by $d$ everywhere). In order to see this, it suffices to pick only one element in the corresponding metric projection. So (cf. Step~2 in the proof of Theorem~\ref{t:BV}), choose $y_0\in F(t_0)$ such that $d(x_0,y_0)=d(x_0,F(t_0))$, set $y_0^n:=y_0$, and if $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and elements $y_{i-1}^n\in F(t_{i-1}^n)$ are already chosen, pick \mbox{$y_i^n\in F(t_i^n)$} such that $d(y_{i-1}^n,y_i^n)=d(y_{i-1}^n,F(t_i^n))$. Define $\Gamma_n:T\to M$ (as in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:4+})} and \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:re})}) by $\Gamma_n(t_i^n):=y_i^n$ for $i=0,1,\dots,n$, and $\Gamma_n(t):=y_{i-1}^n$ if $t\in T\cap(t_{i-1}^n,t_i^n)$ and $i=1,\dots,n$. It remains to note (for $T\subset[t_0,b]$) that \begin{align*} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_n,T)&=\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma_n,T\cap[t_{i-1}^n,t_i^n]) =\sum_{i=1}^n d(y_{i-1}^n,y_i^n)\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n d(y_{i-1}^n,F(t_i^n))\le\sum_{i=1}^n e(F(t_{i-1}^n),F(t_i^n)) \le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T). \end{align*} In this way, Theorem~\ref{t:BV} above is a generalization of \cite[Theorem~1]{JMAA07}, treating the existence of single-valued selectors on (connected) intervals $T\subset\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $X_0=\{x_0\}$, choosing single nearest points instead of projections gives single-valued BV selectors, generalizing Chistyakov-Repovš.
nodes.label: r:single

nodes.name: Space $M=\ell_1(\mathbb{N};\mathbb{B})$
nodes.statement: Let $(\mathbb{B},|\cdot|)$ be a Banach space with norm $|\cdot|$ (e.g., $\mathbb{B}=\mathbb{R}$), $\mathbb{B}^\mathbb{N}$ be the set of all sequences $x:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{B}$, and $M=\ell_1(\mathbb{N};\mathbb{B})$ be the (infinite-dimensional) Banach space of all \emph{summable\/} sequences $x\in\mathbb{B}^\mathbb{N}$ equipped with the norm $\|x\|:=\sum_{i=1}^\infty|x(i)|<+\infty$ and, hence, metric $d(x,y):=\|x-y\|$ for $x,y\in M$.

nodes.name: Unit vectors $u_n$
nodes.statement: Fix $u\in\mathbb{B}$ with $|u|=1$ (e.g., $u=1$ in $\mathbb{R}$) and, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, denote by $u_n$ the unit vector in $M$ defined as usual by $u_n(i)=0$ if $i\ne n$, and $u_n(n)=u$.

nodes.name: Bounded closed (noncompact) values: no admissible selector
nodes.statement: A multifunction $F$ on $T\subset\mathbb{R}$ with (only) \emph{bounded closed\/} values in $M$ and ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)<+\infty$ may have no set-valued selectors $\Gamma$ satisfying \begin{equation} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\quad\mbox{or} \quad d_H(X_0,\Gamma(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0)) \end{equation} with $t_0\in T$ and $X_0\in\mbox{c}(M)$. In order to see this, we set $T:=[0,1]$ and $X:=X_0\cup Y$, where $X_0:=\{u_1\}$ and $Y:=\{\alpha_nu_n:n\ge2\}$ with $\alpha_n:=1+(1/n)$, and note that $X$ and $Y$ are bounded and closed (but not compact) subsets of $M$, whereas $X_0\in\mbox{c}(M)$ and $X_0\subset X$. Define $F:T\to\{X,Y\}\subset\mathcal{P}(M)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ by $F(0):=X$ and $F(t):=Y$ if $0<t\le1$. (A similar example was given in \cite[Example~2]{JMAA} for $F$ with $\mbox{\rm V}(F,T)<+\infty$.) We have ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=e(X,Y)$, where \begin{align*} e(X,Y)&=\sup_{x\in X}\inf_{y\in Y}d(x,y)=e(X\setminus Y,Y)=e(X_0,Y)\\ &=\inf_{n\ge2}(|u_1|+\alpha_n|u_n|)=1+\inf_{n\ge2}\Bigl(1+\frac1n\Bigr)=2. \end{align*} Since $Y\subset X$, $F$ is nonincreasing on $T$ (Section~\ref{ss:mon}), and so, ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=0$. (a) Suppose $t_0=0$, so that $T_{[t_0,+\infty)}=T$. We have $X_0\subset X=F(0)$, which implies $e(X_0,F(0))=0$. Let $\Gamma:T\to\mathcal{P}(M)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ be \emph{any\/} set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$ such that $\Gamma(0)=X_0$. Since $\varnothing\ne\Gamma(1)\subset F(1)=Y$, $\alpha_nu_n\in\Gamma(1)$ for some $n\ge2$. It follows that \begin{align*} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&\ge d_H(\Gamma(0),\Gamma(1))\ge e(\Gamma(1),\Gamma(0)) =e(\Gamma(1),X_0)\\[1pt] &\ge d(\alpha_nu_n,u_1)=\alpha_n+1>2={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T). \end{align*} (b) Now, suppose $0<t_0\le1$, and $\Gamma:T\to\mathcal{P}(M)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ is a set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$. Since $\Gamma(t_0)\subset F(t_0)=Y$, we have $\alpha_nu_n\in\Gamma(t_0)$ for some $n\ge2$, and so, \begin{align*} d_H(X_0,\Gamma(t_0))&\ge e(\Gamma(t_0),X_0)\ge d(\alpha_nu_n,u_1) =\alpha_n+1\\[3pt] &>2=e(X_0,Y)=e(X_0,F(t_0)). \end{align*} (c) The effect of nonexistence of set-valued selectors in (a) and (b) above is due to the fact that $\mbox{Pr}_YX_0=\varnothing$ (cf.~\mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Pr})}): indeed, if $y\in Y$, then $y=\alpha_nu_n$ for some $n\ge2$, and so, for $x\in X_0=\{u_1\}$, we have \begin{equation*} d(x,y)=d(u_1,\alpha_nu_n)=1+\alpha_n>2=e(X_0,Y)=d(u_1,Y)=d(x,Y). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: With bounded closed but noncompact values in $\ell_1$, no selector satisfies the variation or initial-value bounds, since a metric projection is empty.
nodes.label: ex1

nodes.name: Selector inequalities (e:zz)
nodes.statement: \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[t_0,+\infty)})\quad\mbox{or} \quad d_H(X_0,\Gamma(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0))
nodes.label: e:zz

nodes.name: Noncompact value at a single point
nodes.statement:
This example is more subtle than Example~ef{ex1}: even if $F(t)$ is bounded and closed (but not compact) at a \emph{single/} point $t\in T$, inequalities \mbox{m(ef{e:zz})} may not hold in Theorem~ef{t:BV} (this is inspired by \cite[Example~5.2]{Sovae}). Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, $N\ge2$, be fixed and $\{\alpha_n\}_{n=1}^\infty\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a sequence such that  egin{equation} \mbox{$\{|\alpha_n|\}_{n=1}^\infty$ \,is \,strictly \,decreasing}\quad \mbox{and}\!\!\quad\inf_{n\ge N+1}|\alpha_n|>0 \end{equation} (e.g., $\alpha_n=\alpha(n+1)/n$ with $\alpha
e0$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$). We set $X:=\{\alpha_nu_n:1\le n\le N\}$ and $Y:=\{\alpha_nu_n:n\ge N+1\}$. Clearly, $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$, while $Y
otin\mbox{c}(M)$ is bounded (by the first condition in \mbox{m(ef{e:C1})}) and closed (by the second condition in \mbox{m(ef{e:C1})}) in $M$. Define $F$ on $T:=[0,1]$ by $F(t)\!:=X$ if $0\le t<1$, and $F(1)\!:=Y$. We have  egin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T)=e(X,Y)=|\alpha_1|+\inf_{n\ge N+1}|\alpha_n| \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T)=e(Y,X)=|\alpha_{N+1}|+|\alpha_N|. \end{equation*} (a) Suppose $0\le t_0<1$ and $X_0:=\{\alpha_1u_1\}$, so that $T_{[t_0,+\infty)}=[t_0,1]$ and $X_0\subset X=F(t_0)$, which implies $e(X_0,F(t_0))=0$. Let $\Gamma:T	o\mathcal{P}(M)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ be a set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$ such that $\Gamma(t_0)=X_0$. Since $\Gamma(1)\subset F(1)=Y$, we find $\alpha_nu_n\in\Gamma(1)$ for some $n\ge N+1$, and so,  egin{align*} \mbox{m V}(\Gamma,[t_0,1])&\ge d_H(\Gamma(t_0),\Gamma(1))\ge e (\Gamma(1),X_0) \ge d(\alpha_nu_n,\alpha_1u_1)=|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_1|\[2pt] &>|\alpha_1|+\inf_{i\ge N+1}|\alpha_i|={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T)={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,[t_0,1]). \end{align*} (b) Suppose $t_0=1$ and $X_0:=\{\alpha_1u_1\}$. If $\Gamma:T	o\mathcal{P}(M)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ is a set-valued selector of $F$ on $T$, then $\Gamma(1)\subset F(1)=Y$ implies $\alpha_nu_n\in\Gamma(1)$ for some $n\ge N+1$, and so,  egin{align*} d_H(X_0,\Gamma(1))&\ge e(\Gamma(1),X_0)\ge d(\alpha_nu_n,\alpha_1u_1) =|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_1|\[2pt] &>|\alpha_1|+\inf_{i\ge N+1}|\alpha_i|=e(X,Y)\ge e(X_0,Y)=e(X_0,F(t_0)). \end{align*} (c) Clearly, $\mbox{Pr}_XX_0=X_0$. The non-existence of set-valued selectors in (a) and (b) is again due to the fact that $\mbox{Pr}_YX_0=\varnothing$: in fact, if $y\in Y$, then $y=\alpha_nu_n$ for some $n\ge N+1$, and so, we have, for $x\in X_0=\{\alpha_1u_1\}$,  egin{equation*} d(x,y)\!=\!d(\alpha_1u_1,\alpha_nu_n)\!=\!|\alpha_1|+|\alpha_n| \!>\!\!\inf_{i\ge N+1}(|\alpha_1|+|\alpha_i|)\!=\!\inf_{y\in Y}d(x,y)\!=\!d(x,Y). \end{equation*} (d) We claim that Theorem~ef{t:BV}(b) holds with $t_0=1$ and $\Gamma(1)=X_0$ (except that $\Gamma(1)\in\mbox{c}(M)$) for every nonempty $X_0\subset Y=F(1)$. First, observe that $\mbox{Pr}_XY_0=\{\alpha_Nu_N\}$ for every $\varnothing
e Y_0\subset Y$ (recall that $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$, and $\mbox{Pr}_XY_0$ is the set of those $x\in X$, for which $d(y_0,x)=d(y_0,X)$ for some $y_0\in Y_0$). To see this, we set $n_0:=\min\{n\ge N+1:\alpha_nu_n\in Y_0\}$ for $Y_0\subset Y$. If $y_0\in Y_0$, we have $y_0=\alpha_nu_n$ for some $n\ge n_0$,  egin{equation*} d(y_0,X)=\inf_{x\in X}d(y_0,x)=\min_{1\le i\le N}(|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_i|) =|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_N|,\[2pt] \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} \mbox{$d(y_0,x)=|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_i|$ \,if \,$x=\alpha_iu_i\in X$ for some $1\le i\le N$.} \end{equation*} If $n=n_0$ and $i=N$, we find $y_0=\alpha_{n_0}u_{n_0}\in Y_0$, $x=\alpha_Nu_N\in X$, and  egin{equation*} d(y_0,x)=d(\alpha_{n_0}u_{n_0},\alpha_Nu_N)=|\alpha_{n_0}|+|\alpha_N|=d(y_0,X), \end{equation*} which implies $\alpha_Nu_N\in\mbox{Pr}_XY_0$. Now, if $i<N$, then $|\alpha_i|>|\alpha_N|$, and so, for every $y_0\in Y_0$, we get  egin{equation*} d(y_0,x)=|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_i|>|\alpha_n|+|\alpha_N|=d(y_0,X). \end{equation*} Thus, $\alpha_iu_i
otin\mbox{Pr}_XY_0$ for all $i=1,\dots,N-1$, and we are through. Taking the above into account, define a set-valued selector $\Gamma$ of $F$ on $T$ by $\Gamma(t):=\{\alpha_Nu_N\}$ if $0\le t<1$, and $\Gamma(1):=X_0$ with $X_0=Y_0\subset Y$. It remains to note that $n_0\ge N+1$ implies  egin{align*} {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(\Gamma,T)&=e(Y_0,\{\alpha_Nu_N\})=\sup_{y_0\in Y_0}d(y_0,\alpha_Nu_N) =|\alpha_{n_0}|+|\alpha_N|\ &\le|\alpha_{N+1}|+|\alpha_N|={\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{m V}}}(F,T). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A single noncompact value already breaks the inequalities of Theorem 1, though Theorem 1(b) can still hold.
nodes.label: ex2

nodes.name: Conditions on $\alpha_n$ (e:C1)
nodes.statement: \mbox{$\{|\alpha_n|\}_{n=1}^\infty$ \,is \,strictly \,decreasing}\quad \mbox{and}\!\!\quad\inf_{n\ge N+1}|\alpha_n|>0
nodes.label: e:C1

nodes.name: Finite right variation, infinite left variation
nodes.statement: Making use of an idea from \cite[Example~3.1]{JMAA07}, here we present an example of a multifunction $F:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ with $T:=[0,1]$ such that ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)<+\infty$ and ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=+\infty$ (thus, Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a) is applicable to $F$, whereas Theorem~\ref{t:A} is not). Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\{\alpha_n\}_{n=1}^\infty\subset(0,+\infty)$ be a decreasing sequence such that \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\alpha_n=0\quad\mbox{and}\quad \sum_{n=1}^\infty\alpha_{nN}=+\infty \end{equation} (e.g., $\alpha_n=1/n$). Given $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we set \begin{equation*} X_n:=\{0\}\cup\{\alpha_iu_i:1\le i\le nN\},\quad\mbox{and}\quad X_\infty:=\{0\}\cup\{\alpha_iu_i:i\in\mathbb{N}\}. \end{equation*} Clearly, $X_n\in\mbox{c}(M)$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and, by the first assumption in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Alph})}, the set $X_\infty$ is compact as well. Let $\{\tau_n\}_{n=0}^\infty\subset[0,1)$ be a strictly increasing sequence such that $\tau_0=0$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty}\tau_n=1$. Define $F:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ by the rule: \begin{equation*} \mbox{$F(t):=X_n$ \,if\, $\tau_{n-1}\le t<\tau_n$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, \,and\, $F(1):=X_\infty$.} \end{equation*} Since $X_n\subset X_{n+1}\subset X_\infty$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $F$ is nondecreasing on $T$ (Section~\ref{ss:mon}), and so, ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=0$. In order to see that ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=+\infty$, given $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $m\ge2$, and partition $\pi_m=\{\tau_n\}_{n=0}^{m-1}\cup\{1\}$ of $T=[0,1]$, we find \begin{align} {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)&\ge\sum_{n=1}^{m-1}e(F(\tau_n),F(\tau_{n-1}))+e(F(1),F(\tau_{m-1})) \nonumber\\ &=\sum_{n=1}^{m-1}e(X_{n+1},X_n)+e(X_\infty,X_m), \end{align} where \begin{equation*} e(X_{n+1},X_n)=\sup_{nN+1\le k\le(n+1)N}\Bigl(|\alpha_k|+ \inf_{1\le i\le nN}|\alpha_i|\Bigr)=\alpha_{nN+1}+\alpha_{nN} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} e(X_\infty,X_m)=\sup_{k\ge mN+1}\Bigl(|\alpha_k|+ \inf_{1\le i\le mN}|\alpha_i|\Bigr)=\alpha_{mN+1}+\alpha_{mN}. \end{equation*} It follows that the quantity \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:rhs})} is equal to \begin{equation*} \sum_{n=1}^m\alpha_{nN+1}+\sum_{n=1}^m\alpha_{nN}\to+\infty\quad \mbox{as}\quad m\to\infty. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: A nondecreasing compact-valued $F$ on $[0,1]$ with $\vec V=0$ and $\overleftarrow V=\infty$: Theorem 1(a) applies but Theorem A does not.
nodes.label: ex3

nodes.name: Conditions on $\alpha_n$ (e:Alph)
nodes.statement: \lim_{n\to\infty}\alpha_n=0\quad\mbox{and}\quad \sum_{n=1}^\infty\alpha_{nN}=+\infty
nodes.label: e:Alph

nodes.name: Lower bound for left variation (e:rhs)
nodes.statement: {\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)&\ge\sum_{n=1}^{m-1}e(F(\tau_n),F(\tau_{n-1}))+e(F(1),F(\tau_{m-1})) \nonumber\\ &=\sum_{n=1}^{m-1}e(X_{n+1},X_n)+e(X_\infty,X_m),
nodes.label: e:rhs

nodes.name: Initial point and jump term are essential
nodes.statement: (a) By Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a), given $X_0\in\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_0\subset X_1=F(0)$, multifunction $F$ from Example~\ref{ex3} has a constant set-valued selector $\Gamma:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ satisfying $\Gamma(0)=X_0$ and $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=0$. However, if $0<t_0\le1$ and $X_0\subset F(t_0)$, there may be no set-valued selector $\Gamma$ of $F$ on $T$ such that $\Gamma(t_0)=X_0$ and $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)$. In fact, let $t_0=\tau_n$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$ (cf. Example~\ref{ex3}), so that $F(t_0)=F(\tau_n)=X_{n+1}$. Suppose now that $X_0\subset X_{n+1}\setminus X_1\subset F(t_0)$, $\Gamma(t)\subset F(t)$ for all $t\in T$, and $\Gamma(t_0)=X_0$. Since $\Gamma(0)\subset F(0)=X_1$, we have $\alpha_iu_i\in\Gamma(0)$ for some $1\le i\le N$, or $0\in\Gamma(0)$ (i.e., possibly, $\alpha_i=0$), and so, \begin{align} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&\ge d_H(\Gamma(t_0),\Gamma(0))=d_H(X_0,\Gamma(0)) \ge e(\Gamma(0),X_0)\nonumber\\[3pt] &\ge d(\alpha_iu_i,X_0)\ge d(\alpha_iu_i,X_{n+1}\setminus X_1)\nonumber\\[2pt] &=\min_{N+1\le k\le (n+1)N}(\alpha_i+\alpha_k)\ge\alpha_{(n+1)N} >0={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T). \end{align} (b) If $t_0>a=\inf T$ and $\Gamma(t_0)=X_0$, inequality $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0)})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0)})$ in Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a) cannot in general be replaced by $\mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T_{[a,t_0]})\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T_{[a,t_0]})$. This can be seen from Example~\ref{ex4} and \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:519})}: \begin{equation*} \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,[0,t_0])\ge d_H(\Gamma(t_0),\Gamma(0))\ge\dots\ge \alpha_{(n+1)N}>0={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,[0,t_0]). \end{equation*} This observation also makes it explicit that the ``jump'' $J_a(\Gamma,t_0)$ is essential in the left-hand side of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:s1t0})}.
nodes.statement_short: For $t_0>0$ no selector of Example 3 meets $V(\Gamma,T)\le\vec V(F,T)$; the jump $J_a$ in (e:s1t0) cannot be dropped.
nodes.label: ex4

nodes.name: Lower bound (e:519)
nodes.statement: \mbox{\rm V}(\Gamma,T)&\ge d_H(\Gamma(t_0),\Gamma(0))=d_H(X_0,\Gamma(0)) \ge e(\Gamma(0),X_0)\nonumber\\[3pt] &\ge d(\alpha_iu_i,X_0)\ge d(\alpha_iu_i,X_{n+1}\setminus X_1)\nonumber\\[2pt] &=\min_{N+1\le k\le (n+1)N}(\alpha_i+\alpha_k)\ge\alpha_{(n+1)N} >0={\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T).
nodes.label: e:519

nodes.name: Image not totally bounded under bounded right variation
nodes.statement: This example is designed for Remark~\ref{p:7}. Let $T:=[1,+\infty)$ and $F:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ be given by $F(t)\!:=\!X_n$ if $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\le t<n+1$, where $X_n\!:=\!\{u_i:1\le i\le n\}$. We have $X_n\in\mbox{c}(M)$, and $F(s)\subset F(t)$ for all $1\le s\le t<+\infty$, and so, ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=0$. The image \mbox{$F(T)=\bigcup_{n=1}^\infty X_n=\{u_i:i\in\mathbb{N}\}$} is bounded in $M$, but \emph{not\/} totally bounded (i.e., cannot be covered by a finite number of balls of arbitrarily small radius). Note that ${\scriptstyle\overleftarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F,T)=+\infty$ (consider a partition $1<2<\dots<m-1<m$ of $T$ with arbitrary $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and observe that $e(X_{n+1},X_n)=2$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$). This example is easily adapted to the case when $F$ maps $[a,b)$ or $[a,b]$ into~$\mbox{c}(M)$.
nodes.statement_short: $F(t)=\{u_1,\dots,u_n\}$ on $[n,n+1)$: $\vec V=0$ but $F(T)$ is not totally bounded.
nodes.label: ex:5.5

nodes.name: Existence of BV solutions to the functional inclusion $X(t)\subset F(t,X(t))$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: First, observe that assumptions (a) and (b) and the triangle inequality for $e$ imply, for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$, and $X,Y\in\mbox{c}(M)$, \begin{equation} e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y). \end{equation} We set $X_0(t)\!:=\!X_0$ and $F_0(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_0)$ for $t\in T$. We have \mbox{$F_0:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$}, and assumption (a) and Lemma~\ref{l:char} imply ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_0,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)<+\infty$. By Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a), there is $X_1\equiv\Gamma:T=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_1(t)\subset F_0(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_0(t_0))$, and $\mbox{\rm V}(X_1,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_0,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)$. In what follows we apply the standard iteration procedure. Setting $F_1(t):=F(t,X_1(t))$ for $t\in T$, we find $F_1:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, \begin{equation*} e(F_1(s),F_1(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_1(s),X_1(t))\quad \forall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t. \end{equation*} Arguing with partitions of $T$, Lemma~\ref{l:char} implies \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_1,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)+\mu\mbox{\rm V}(X_1,T)\le(1+\mu)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Applying Theorem~\ref{t:BV} again, we obtain $X_2:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_2(t)\subset F_1(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))$, and \begin{equation*} \mbox{\rm V}(X_2,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_1,T)\le(1+\mu)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} If $F_2(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_2(t))$, $t\in T$, then $F_2:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, \begin{equation*} e(F_2(s),F_2(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_2(s),X_2(t))\quad \forall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t, \end{equation*} and so, \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_2,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)+\mu\mbox{\rm V}(X_2,T)\le(1+\mu+\mu^2)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Arguing by induction, we obtain the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of multifunctions $X_n:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that, given $n\in\mathbb{N}$, \begin{eqnarray} &X_n(t)\subset F_{n-1}(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\subset K(t)\quad\mbox{for all $t\in T$,}& \\[3pt] &d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_{n-1}(t_0))\!=\!e\bigl(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0))\bigr), \,\,\mbox{and}& \\ &\displaystyle\mbox{\rm V}(X_n,T)\le\biggl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mu^i\biggr)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T) \le\frac1{1-\mu}\,\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T).& \end{eqnarray} By \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vft})}, the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is of uniformly bounded Jordan variation with respect to $d_H$, and so, condition (a) in Theorem~\ref{t:B} is satisfied, and by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Xnt})}, the closure $\ov{\{X_n(t):n\in\mathbb{N}\}}$ in $\mbox{c}(M)$ is compact for every $t\in T$, and so, condition (b) in Theorem~\ref{t:B} is fulfiled. By Theorem~\ref{t:B}, a subsequence of $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, again denoted by $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, converges in $\mbox{c}(M)$ pointwise on $T$ to a multifunction $X:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$, i.e., $d_H(X_n(t),X(t))\to0$ as $n\to\infty$ for all $t\in T$. We are going to verify that $X$ satisfies assertions (i), (ii), and (iii). Assertion (i) is a consequence of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vft})} and the lower semicontinuity \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vsem})} of~$\mbox{\rm V}$. In order to see that (ii) holds, we make use of the following inequality (cf. \cite[inequality~(11.7)]{Sovae}), which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$: \begin{equation} |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y'). \end{equation} In fact, given $t\in T$, \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Xnt})} implies $e\bigl(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\bigr)=0$, and so, taking into account \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Sog})} and \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, we get \begin{align*} e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))&\!=\!\bigl|e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))\!-\!e(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\bigr|\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!d_H(F(t,X(t)),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!\mu d_H(X(t),X_{n-1}(t))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Thus, $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$, which implies (by properties of~$e$) assertion~(ii). To establish (iii), we note that (cf. \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})} and (iii)) \begin{equation*} |d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))-d_H(X_0,X(t_0))|\le d_H(X_n(t_0),X(t_0))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty, \end{equation*} and, by virtue of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Sog})} and assumption (b), \begin{align*} &\qquad\bigl|e(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)))-e(X_0,F(t_0,X(t_0)))\bigr|\\[2pt] \le&\,d_H(F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)),F(t_0,X(t_0)))\le\mu d_H(X_{n-1}(t_0),X(t_0)) \to0,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Passing to the limit as $n\to\infty$ in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})}, we arrive at~(iii). Finally, suppose $X_0\!\subset\! F(t_0,X_0)$. Hence $X_0\!\subset\! F_0(t_0)$ and $e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$. From the above, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$, and so, $X_1(t_0)\!=\!X_0$. Since \begin{equation*} X_0\subset F_0(t_0)=F(t_0,X_0)=F(t_0,X_1(t_0))=F_1(t_0), \end{equation*} we find from $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))=0$ that $X_2(t_0)=X_0$. By induction, we deduce from \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})} that $X_n(t_0)=X_0$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Passing to the lmit as $n\to\infty$ in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})}, we get $d_H(X_0,X(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0,X_0))=0$, which yields $X(t_0)=X_0$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Iterate: $X_{n}$ is a BV selector (Theorem 1(a)) of $F(\cdot,X_{n-1}(\cdot))$ with geometric variation bounds; Theorem B gives a pointwise limit, which solves the inclusion.

nodes.name: Joint excess estimate (e:XY)
nodes.statement: e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y).
nodes.label: e:XY

nodes.name: Iteration properties (e:Xnt), (e:Hot), (e:Vft)
nodes.statement: &X_n(t)\subset F_{n-1}(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\subset K(t)\quad\mbox{for all $t\in T$,}& \\[3pt] &d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_{n-1}(t_0))\!=\!e\bigl(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0))\bigr), \,\,\mbox{and}& \\ &\displaystyle\mbox{\rm V}(X_n,T)\le\biggl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mu^i\biggr)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T) \le\frac1{1-\mu}\,\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T).&
nodes.label: e:Xnt

nodes.name: Excess Lipschitz inequality (e:Sog)
nodes.statement: |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y').
nodes.label: e:Sog

nodes.name: Joint excess estimate
nodes.statement: First, observe that assumptions (a) and (b) and the triangle inequality for $e$ imply, for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$, and $X,Y\in\mbox{c}(M)$, \begin{equation} e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine (a), (b) and the excess triangle inequality.

nodes.name: First iterate
nodes.statement: We set $X_0(t)\!:=\!X_0$ and $F_0(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_0)$ for $t\in T$. We have \mbox{$F_0:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$}, and assumption (a) and Lemma~\ref{l:char} imply ${\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_0,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)<+\infty$. By Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a), there is $X_1\equiv\Gamma:T=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_1(t)\subset F_0(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_0(t_0))$, and $\mbox{\rm V}(X_1,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_0,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 and Theorem 1(a) give $X_1$.

nodes.name: Next iterates
nodes.statement: In what follows we apply the standard iteration procedure. Setting $F_1(t):=F(t,X_1(t))$ for $t\in T$, we find $F_1:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, \begin{equation*} e(F_1(s),F_1(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_1(s),X_1(t))\quad \forall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t. \end{equation*} Arguing with partitions of $T$, Lemma~\ref{l:char} implies \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_1,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)+\mu\mbox{\rm V}(X_1,T)\le(1+\mu)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Applying Theorem~\ref{t:BV} again, we obtain $X_2:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_2(t)\subset F_1(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))$, and \begin{equation*} \mbox{\rm V}(X_2,T)\le{\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_1,T)\le(1+\mu)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} If $F_2(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_2(t))$, $t\in T$, then $F_2:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, \begin{equation*} e(F_2(s),F_2(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_2(s),X_2(t))\quad \forall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t, \end{equation*} and so, \begin{equation*} {\scriptstyle\overrightarrow{\mbox{\rm V}}}(F_2,T)\le\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)+\mu\mbox{\rm V}(X_2,T)\le(1+\mu+\mu^2)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\vec V(F_n,T)$ geometrically and reapply Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Induction
nodes.statement: Arguing by induction, we obtain the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of multifunctions $X_n:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$ such that, given $n\in\mathbb{N}$, \begin{eqnarray} &X_n(t)\subset F_{n-1}(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\subset K(t)\quad\mbox{for all $t\in T$,}& \\[3pt] &d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_{n-1}(t_0))\!=\!e\bigl(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0))\bigr), \,\,\mbox{and}& \\ &\displaystyle\mbox{\rm V}(X_n,T)\le\biggl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mu^i\biggr)\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T) \le\frac1{1-\mu}\,\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T).& \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Sequence $X_n$ with (e:Xnt)-(e:Vft).

nodes.name: Extract a limit
nodes.statement: By \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vft})}, the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is of uniformly bounded Jordan variation with respect to $d_H$, and so, condition (a) in Theorem~\ref{t:B} is satisfied, and by \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Xnt})}, the closure $\ov{\{X_n(t):n\in\mathbb{N}\}}$ in $\mbox{c}(M)$ is compact for every $t\in T$, and so, condition (b) in Theorem~\ref{t:B} is fulfiled. By Theorem~\ref{t:B}, a subsequence of $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, again denoted by $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, converges in $\mbox{c}(M)$ pointwise on $T$ to a multifunction $X:T\to\mbox{c}(M)$, i.e., $d_H(X_n(t),X(t))\to0$ as $n\to\infty$ for all $t\in T$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem B gives a pointwise convergent subsequence.

nodes.name: Assertion (i)
nodes.statement: We are going to verify that $X$ satisfies assertions (i), (ii), and (iii). Assertion (i) is a consequence of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vft})} and the lower semicontinuity \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Vsem})} of~$\mbox{\rm V}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity of $V$ gives (i).

nodes.name: Assertion (ii)
nodes.statement: In order to see that (ii) holds, we make use of the following inequality (cf. \cite[inequality~(11.7)]{Sovae}), which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$: \begin{equation} |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y'). \end{equation} In fact, given $t\in T$, \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Xnt})} implies $e\bigl(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\bigr)=0$, and so, taking into account \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Sog})} and \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:XY})}, we get \begin{align*} e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))&\!=\!\bigl|e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))\!-\!e(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\bigr|\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!d_H(F(t,X(t)),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!\mu d_H(X(t),X_{n-1}(t))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Thus, $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$, which implies (by properties of~$e$) assertion~(ii).
nodes.statement_short: Excess Lipschitz inequality (e:Sog) and contraction give $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$.

nodes.name: Assertion (iii)
nodes.statement: To establish (iii), we note that (cf. \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})} and (iii)) \begin{equation*} |d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))-d_H(X_0,X(t_0))|\le d_H(X_n(t_0),X(t_0))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty, \end{equation*} and, by virtue of \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Sog})} and assumption (b), \begin{align*} &\qquad\bigl|e(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)))-e(X_0,F(t_0,X(t_0)))\bigr|\\[2pt] \le&\,d_H(F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)),F(t_0,X(t_0)))\le\mu d_H(X_{n-1}(t_0),X(t_0)) \to0,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Passing to the limit as $n\to\infty$ in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})}, we arrive at~(iii).
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit in (e:Hot).

nodes.name: Exact initial condition
nodes.statement: Finally, suppose $X_0\!\subset\! F(t_0,X_0)$. Hence $X_0\!\subset\! F_0(t_0)$ and $e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$. From the above, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$, and so, $X_1(t_0)\!=\!X_0$. Since \begin{equation*} X_0\subset F_0(t_0)=F(t_0,X_0)=F(t_0,X_1(t_0))=F_1(t_0), \end{equation*} we find from $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))=0$ that $X_2(t_0)=X_0$. By induction, we deduce from \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})} that $X_n(t_0)=X_0$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Passing to the lmit as $n\to\infty$ in \mbox{\rm(\ref{e:Hot})}, we get $d_H(X_0,X(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0,X_0))=0$, which yields $X(t_0)=X_0$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By induction $X_n(t_0)=X_0$, hence $X(t_0)=X_0$.

nodes.name: Special cases of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: If $F(t,X)=F(t)$ is independent of $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$ (or $\mu=0$), Theorem~ \ref{t:FuEm} gives back Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a): we may set $\varphi=\ori{v}_{F}$ and~$K=F$. On the other hand, if $F(t,X)=F(X)$ is independent of $t\in T$ (or $\varphi\equiv0$), Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} is a consequence of Banach's Contraction Theorem (in fact, $F:\mbox{c}(K)\to\mbox{c}(K)$ is a contraction on compact, hence complete, metric space $(\mbox{c}(K),d_H)$ with $K=K(t_0)$).
nodes.statement_short: If $F$ is independent of $X$, Theorem 2 gives Theorem 1(a); if independent of $t$, it follows from Banach's contraction theorem.

nodes.name: Scaling multifunction satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The purpose of this example is to show that assumptions of Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} can be fulfiled. Let $M=\mathbb{B}$ be a Banach space with norm $|\cdot|$ and metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|$, $x,y\in M$, and $K\in\mbox{c}(M)$. Suppose $\varphi_0:T\to[0,+\infty)$ is nondecreasing and $\mu\!:=\!\sup_{t\in T}\varphi_0(t)<1$. Define $F:T\times\mbox{c}(M)\to\mbox{c}(M)$ by $F(t,X):=\varphi_0(t)X$ for $t\in T$ and $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$. We have \begin{equation*} e(F(s,X),F(t,X))\le\bigl(\varphi_0(t)-\varphi_0(s)\bigr)\max_{x\in X}|x|\quad \mbox{for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$,} \end{equation*} and so, condition (a) in Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} is satisfied with $\varphi(t)\!:=\!\varphi_0(t)\max_{x\in K}|x|$, $t\in T$, for all $X\in\mbox{c}(K)$. Furthermore, given $t\in T$ and $X,Y\in\mbox{c}(K)\subset\mbox{c}(M)$, \begin{equation*} e(F(t,X),F(t,Y))=\varphi_0(t)e(X,Y)\le\mu d_H(X,Y), \end{equation*} and so, condition (b) in Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} is satisfied. Finally, setting $K(t):=\varphi_0(t)K$, we find $F(t,X)\subset K(t)$ for all $t\in T$ and $X\in\mbox{c}(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: $F(t,X)=\varphi_0(t)X$ in a Banach space satisfies conditions (a)-(c) of Theorem 2.
nodes.label: ex:6.1

nodes.name: Cantor-type set-valued solutions
nodes.statement: In Example~\ref{ex:6.1}, we set $\mathbb{B}:=\mathbb{R}$, $K:=[0,1]$, and $\varphi_0(t):=t$ for $t\in T:=[0,1/2]$ (hence $\mu=1/2$, $\varphi=\varphi_0$, and $\mbox{\rm V}(\varphi,T)=1/2$). Define $F$ by \begin{equation*} F(t,X):=(tX)\cup(1-t+tX),\quad t\in T,\,\,X\in\mbox{c}(K). \end{equation*} For instance, if $X=[0,1]$, we have $F(0,X)=\{0,1\}$, $F(1/2,X)=[0,1]$, and if $0<t<1/2$, then $F(t,X)=[0,t]\cup[1-t,1]$, $F(t,[0,t])=[0,t^2]\cup[1-t,1-t+t^2]$, $F(t,[1-t,1])=[t-t^2,t]\cup[1-t^2,1]$, and so on. The iterative construction of the classical Cantor (ternary) set corresponds to $t=1/3$ (e.g., \cite[p.~20]{GK}). By Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm}, there is $X:[0,1/2]\to\mbox{c}([0,1])$ such that $\mbox{\rm V}(X,[0,1/2])\!\le\!1$, $X(t)\subset(tX(t))\cup(1-t+tX(t))$ for all $t\in[0,1/2]$, and $X(0)=\{0,1\}$. For every $t\in(0,1/2)$, the compact set $X(t)\subset[0,1]$ is a Cantor-type perfect set.
nodes.statement_short: $F(t,X)=tX\cup(1-t+tX)$ on $[0,1/2]$ yields BV solutions whose values are Cantor-type perfect sets.
